result.summary: Adds script and functional test cases covering the 1,000-element stack size limit boundary during P2SH execution. It tests that when a scriptSig leaves 1,000 items on the stack, the 20-byte hash push during scriptPubKey evaluation triggers a STACK_SIZE failure, whereas leaving 999 items succeeds. It also adds a spender to the taproot functional test so the transaction can be exported into QA script test assets.
result.problem: Existing test vectors omit coverage for scriptSigs that push the stack to the 1,000-item limit before the P2SH scriptPubKey runs. As a result, non-compliant Bitcoin implementations that check redeemScript hashes directly without executing the scriptPubKey against the stack can pass all existing test vectors despite erroneously accepting invalid 1,000-item spends.
evidence: PR description: "An implementation that checks the redeemScript hash without running the scriptPubKey accepts the 1,000-item spend. No existing vector leaves the scriptSig at this boundary, so such an implementation can pass every row."
PR description: "These were discovered by finding gaps in an alternate implementation (rbitcoin)"
result.changed_since_previous: Diff provided matches the previous description; no changes to commits or scope.
result.card: Adds test vectors verifying P2SH script evaluation behavior at the 1,000-item stack size limit boundary. Existing script test vectors do not test this boundary, allowing alternative node implementations that verify the redeemScript hash without executing the scriptPubKey to pass all test cases while accepting invalid 1,000-item spends. The PR adds 999- and 1,000-item test rows to script tests and a spender to the functional tests for export to qa-assets.

risk.why: Touches only script and functional test suites without modifying node consensus or validation logic.
